SELECT id, path, parent_id, name FROM lix_directory ORDER BY path LIMIT 100;

WITH RECURSIVE directory_tree(top_id, directory_id) AS (
      SELECT id, id
      FROM lix_directory
      WHERE parent_id IS NULL
      UNION ALL
      SELECT directory_tree.top_id, child.id
      FROM directory_tree
      JOIN lix_directory AS child
        ON child.parent_id = directory_tree.directory_id
    )
    SELECT top.path AS directory_path, COUNT(file.id) AS file_count
    FROM lix_directory AS top
    JOIN directory_tree ON directory_tree.top_id = top.id
    LEFT JOIN lix_file AS file ON file.directory_id = directory_tree.directory_id
    WHERE top.parent_id IS NULL
    GROUP BY top.id, top.path
    ORDER BY top.path;

item.text: The first aggregate hit a SQL parser quirk around an alias; I’m adjusting the query while keeping the hierarchy-ID recursion intact.

statements.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE directory_tree(top_id, directory_id) AS (
      SELECT id, id FROM lix_directory WHERE parent_id IS NULL
      UNION ALL
      SELECT dt.top_id, child.id
      FROM directory_tree AS dt
      JOIN lix_directory AS child ON child.parent_id = dt.directory_id
    )
    SELECT rootdir.path AS directory_path, COUNT(lf.id) AS file_count
    FROM lix_directory AS rootdir
    JOIN directory_tree AS dt ON dt.top_id = rootdir.id
    LEFT JOIN lix_file AS lf ON lf.directory_id = dt.directory_id
    WHERE rootdir.parent_id IS NULL
    GROUP BY rootdir.id, rootdir.path
    ORDER BY rootdir.path;

    )
    SELECT rootdir.path AS directory_path, COUNT(lf.id) AS file_count

    JOIN directory_tree AS dt ON dt.top_id = rootdir.id
    LEFT JOIN lix_file AS lf ON lf.directory_id = dt.directory_id
    WHERE rootdir.parent_id IS NULL
